match: KEYWORDS: no keyword phrase is covered by the first 100 words
why: Adjudicated 2026-09-18, won't fix. The first 100 words of a service page are breadcrumb + eyebrow + h1 + lede + spec chips + the hero figure. Eyebrow, h1, lede and chips are byte-siblings of the /ai panel COPY (another repo, owner-approved wording, just rewritten to grade 6); the figure caption is a designed 11px uppercase label that a keyword phrase would wrap to three lines on a phone. Every one of these pages carries its primary phrase in the <title>, the meta description and the URL (the three checks above this one, all passing), and in the body below the fold. The rule of thumb is not worth sibling drift or a worse hero. Revisit only if the /ai panels are rewritten again: put the phrase in COPY.p there and mirror it.

match: KEYWORDS: <title> shares 0 words with the slug
why: Adjudicated 2026-11-17 (agents round 33), a decision with its reason: this post's address is indexed and is not renamed (agents round 32: the one post that was renamed fell out of Google's index and was still out 17 days later). The post was re-aimed that day on data: its old phrase, 'AI scheduling assistant', is a search for a personal calendar app (Microsoft, the New York Times and calendar apps hold its first page), and 'appointment confirmation text' is searched 100 to 1,000 times a month in the United States (Google Ads Keyword Planner). The title that ships, 'Appointment Confirmation Texts: Three Wordings to Copy', was clicked first in 2 of 2 lists by the blind reader, with the planted poor title clicked in neither. A title that shared three words with the address would have to say 'AI scheduling' and 'showing', and that names the reader the page no longer writes for. Record: realtylt-agents company/agents/seo/runs/r33-retarget/ (PHRASES.md, posts/RECORD.md item 3).
